domain: Regulatory perimeter, mandate design and tax framework for a ₹500 Cr NDPMS mandate (SEBI PMS Regulations 2020, LVAI route, FY2026-27 tax, RBI/FEMA international routes)
executive_summary: Decision 1 — on-board every investing entity of the client as a Large Value Accredited Investor (accredited + ≥₹10 Cr agreement). It is the only route that lets us write a bespoke NDPMS agreement (Schedule IV not mandatory), negotiate exit load, lift the 25% unlisted cap to 100% (we self-cap at 15%), and qualify the client for AIF co-investment (CIV) schemes. Decision 2 — the client "direction" required for NDPMS becomes a monthly Rebalance Proposal Pack (RPP) e-approved on a portal with a hashed audit trail, plus a narrow Standing Instructions Register for mechanical actions (cash sweeps, distribution reinvestment, pre-approved tranche schedules, hedge rolls). Anything that changes weights or names a new security goes through the RPP; a generic "model + bands" approval where we pick names and sizes risks recharacterisation as discretion — get a legal opinion/SEBI informal guidance before go-live. Decision 3 — structure third-party PMS and offshore (LRS/IFSC) sleeves OUTSIDE NDPMS AUM: a PMS is a service not a security, Reg 24 bars investing on another entity's advice (SEBI's May-2026 First Global order makes this bite), and foreign securities are not yet permitted inside PMS (July-2026 consultation only). Decision 4 — tax-aware plumbing: FIFO is per demat account, so run 2–3 purpose-segregated demat accounts; prefer listed bonds/G-secs over debt MFs (12.5% vs ~39%); never realise equity STCG to rebalance without a quantified hurdle; SGB secondary purchases lost their exemption in Budget 2026. Key constants: unlisted ≤25% (100% LVAI); associates 15/25/30% with one-time consent; derivatives ≤1x, hedging/rebalancing only, no leverage; fees: no upfront, opex ≤0.50%, HWM performance fee; reports to client ≤ quarterly (we do monthly), SEBI monthly within 7 working days; MF overseas cap USD 7 bn near-exhausted; LRS USD 250k/adult ≈ ₹2.2 Cr.

can_do.item: On-board all client entities as Large Value Accredited Investors (LVAI)
can_do.what: Accreditation via BSE/NSE/NSDL/CDSL agencies; each entity signs an NDPMS agreement ≥ ₹10 Cr; disclose LVAI terms in the Disclosure Document
can_do.why: Unlocks bespoke agreement (Schedule IV not mandatory), negotiated exit load, unlisted up to 100%, CIV co-investment eligibility
can_do.notes: Accreditation validity 1–2 years approx.; re-accredit on schedule; Jan-2026 net-worth certificate format

can_do.item: Monthly Rebalance Proposal Pack (RPP) as the legal client direction
can_do.what: Portal-delivered trade list (ISIN, side, qty/₹, execution rule, window, cost/tax estimate, band check); client e-signs pack or lines; 10-trading-day validity; hashed audit trail linked to OMS time-stamps
can_do.why: Satisfies 'in accordance with the directions of the client' and the Master Circular audit-trail rules while batching consent to one event per month

can_do.item: Standing Instructions Register for mechanical actions
can_do.what: Revocable, fully specified instructions: daily sweep of idle cash > ₹50 lakh to a named liquid fund, distribution reinvestment, execution of already-approved tranche schedules, auto-roll of approved hedges at same notional
can_do.why: Removes per-trade friction on actions with no investment judgment
can_do.notes: Obtain legal opinion and consider SEBI Informal Guidance; keep instructions limit-order-like, never 'PM decides name/size'

can_do.item: Consent SLA of 2 business days with 48-hour escalation
can_do.what: Agreement clause: RPP sent T-1, approval target T+2, RM escalation call at 48 h, unexecuted lines lapse after 10 trading days
can_do.why: Latency cost: ₹25 Cr under-deployment at 1% daily vol costs ~₹79 lakh 1-sigma over 10 days vs ~₹35 lakh over 2 days

can_do.item: Keep total unlisted (AIF/unlisted InvIT/pre-IPO) at ≤ 15% of AUM by IPS
can_do.what: Legal ceiling 25% (100% LVAI); IPS cap 15% (₹75 Cr) with 10-pt buffer; rights subscriptions only via RPP (active breach risk)
can_do.why: Passive breaches after equity drawdowns and AIF drawdown timing otherwise push past 25%; buffer protects the non-LVAI entities

can_do.item: Group/associate securities capped at 10% of AUM by IPS with SEBI Annexure A consent
can_do.what: One-time prior positive consent at onboarding; alert-based monitoring; IC minute evidencing best-selection for every Angel One group product; disclosure in monthly report
can_do.why: SEBI limits are 15% single / 25% all / 30% combined; conflicts scrutiny is high for a captive wealth arm

can_do.item: Third-party PMS strategies structured outside NDPMS AUM
can_do.what: Client signs directly with external PM; Ionic acts as disclosed distributor or advises; consolidated look-through reporting only
can_do.why: PMS is a service not a security; Reg 24 prohibits investing on another entity's advice (First Global order, May 2026)
can_do.notes: Where the same strategy exists as AIF Cat III or SIF, use the wrapper inside AUM instead

can_do.item: Use SIF units and MF direct plans as the alpha wrapper
can_do.what: SIF (long-short, sector rotation) ₹10 lakh min per PAN per AMC; MF/SIF units are 'mutual fund units' and outside the 25% unlisted cap (interpretation, verify); direct plans only, no distribution fee
can_do.why: Cheapest compliant access to active/long-short exposure without derivatives consent overhead

can_do.item: Derivatives only as a pre-approved tail-hedge protocol
can_do.what: Monthly RPP approves Nifty put-spread notional ≤ 25% of AUM, premium budget ≤ 1% p.a. (₹5 Cr); total exposure ≤ portfolio funds; no leverage; roll via standing instruction
can_do.why: Hedging/rebalancing is the only permitted derivative purpose; options STT now 0.15% of premium

can_do.item: Securities lending through SLB on large-cap core holdings
can_do.what: Client authorisation annex; lend only through exchange SLB; cap 20% of any position
can_do.why: Permitted carve-out under Reg 24; incremental 0.5–3% p.a. on lent lots approx.

can_do.item: Client-name demat and bank accounts under our custodian, no pooling
can_do.what: Dedicated accounts per entity; custodian holds all listed and demat AIF units; daily reconciliation
can_do.why: Custodian is mandatory at this AUM; segregation rules; simplifies inspection

can_do.item: Purpose-segregated demat accounts (Core / Tactical / Income) for FIFO management
can_do.what: Rebalance sells routed from the Tactical account so FIFO consumes lots already past 12 months; separate MF folios by purpose
can_do.why: India mandates FIFO per demat account; specific-ID lot selection is not available

can_do.item: In-specie transfer-in of existing holdings at onboarding
can_do.what: Transfer securities into the NDPMS demat with cost and acquisition dates captured at custodian; no sale
can_do.why: Avoids a tax event on day one; preserves LTCG holding periods

can_do.item: Tax-aware rebalance hurdle rule
can_do.what: Do not realise equity STCG unless expected alpha of the switch > (23.92% − 14.95%) × unrealised gain / proceeds; deploy flows and distributions before selling
can_do.why: Every 1% of AUM realised as STCG costs ~24 bps of NAV vs ~15 bps as LTCG

can_do.item: Fixed income via listed bonds/G-secs/SDLs held > 12 months, not debt MFs
can_do.what: Debt MF gains are slab-taxed (~39%); listed paper gets 12.5% LTCG after 12 m; avoid unlisted debt (deemed STCG)
can_do.why: Saves ~26 pts of tax on gains in the ₹75 Cr fixed-income sleeve

can_do.item: Arbitrage funds for cash parked > 6 months
can_do.what: Equity-oriented taxation (12.5% LTCG after 12 m, 20% STCG) vs slab on liquid funds
can_do.why: Cash sleeve ₹37.5 Cr; tax saving ~15–19 pts on gains

can_do.item: Gold via ETFs; SGB only as primary subscriber (if issuance resumes)
can_do.what: Budget 2026 limited the SGB redemption exemption to original subscribers holding to maturity; secondary-market SGBs are taxed like listed securities
can_do.why: Removes the historic reason to buy SGBs in secondary market

can_do.item: International sleeve inside AUM only via Indian-listed international ETFs/FoFs at ≤ 1% premium to iNAV
can_do.what: Buy rule on premium; monitor AMC overseas-cap windows; sleeve target 7.5% but year-1 realistic ₹10–15 Cr inside AUM
can_do.why: USD 7 bn industry cap near exhaustion; suspended creations cause 5–15% premiums approx.

can_do.item: Family LRS into GIFT-IFSC outbound funds, advised outside AUM
can_do.what: USD 250k per adult per FY (≈ ₹2.2 Cr); 5 adults ≈ ₹11 Cr/yr; TCS 20% above ₹10 lakh creditable; IFSC outbound funds min USD 5,000; IFSC PMS min USD 75,000
can_do.why: Only scalable resident route to direct global exposure today
can_do.notes: Not inside PMS AUM; foreign securities in PMS is a 2026 proposal only

can_do.item: Holding-company OPI into IFSC fund units
can_do.what: Unlisted Indian entity may make OPI in IFSC fund units (Schedule V); listed company may do OPI up to 50% of net worth
can_do.why: Bypasses the LRS ceiling if the family has a corporate vehicle
can_do.notes: Outside AUM; needs FEMA reporting (Form OPI); verify caps for unlisted entities

can_do.item: AIF Cat I/II for private credit and PE with pass-through tax
can_do.what: Cap 5% target / 7.5% max; commitments drawn over 3–4 years; TDS 10% under 194LBB; capital-asset treatment confirmed by Finance Act 2025
can_do.why: Illiquidity premium with client-level taxation; counts in unlisted cap

can_do.item: AIF Cat III only for uncorrelated strategies
can_do.what: Fund-level tax (LTCG 12.5%+, STCG 20%+, F&O/business income at MMR ~39–42.7%); cap 2.5% target / 5% max
can_do.why: Tax inefficiency vs SIF; use only where SIF/MF wrapper unavailable

can_do.item: CIV co-investment alongside AIFs
can_do.what: Accredited-only CIV schemes (Sept 2025 circular): one scheme per deal, ring-fenced, no leverage
can_do.why: Deal-level access for a ₹500 Cr client; fits LVAI status

can_do.item: Fee structure: fixed 0.25–0.40% + 10% performance over house benchmark with HWM, no upfront fee, opex ≤ 0.50%
can_do.what: ₹500 Cr × 0.30% = ₹1.5 Cr fixed + 18% GST; SEBI fee illustration annexure; typed acknowledgement of fees
can_do.why: Regulatory floor plus alignment on alpha
can_do.notes: Fees mostly not deductible against client capital gains — disclose

can_do.item: Monthly client report exceeding Reg 31 minimum
can_do.what: Composition/valuation, transactions, income, expenses, risks, associate exposure, distributor commission, look-through of outside-AUM sleeves, TWRR vs 80/20 house benchmark
can_do.why: Reg 31 allows up to 3 months; monthly builds the audit trail for full ownership of returns

can_do.item: APMI benchmark tagging and daily NDPMS TWRR; annual firm-level performance audit
can_do.what: Tag the NDPMS Investment Approach (multi-asset), select APMI benchmark, compute TWRR daily, include NDPMS in the annual firm-level audit (confirmation to SEBI within 60 days of FY-end); monthly SEBI/APMI report within 7 working days
can_do.why: Mandatory; also the basis for our alpha accountability

can_do.item: Debt/money-market valuation from APMI-empanelled agencies
can_do.what: Daily security-level prices from CRISIL / ICRA Analytics / NSE Indices for all debt in the ₹75 Cr sleeve
can_do.why: Mandatory since 1-Apr-2023; drives NAV and fee base

can_do.item: March tax-loss harvesting and lot-review pack
can_do.what: Identify STCL/LTCL to offset realised gains; re-enter after 1 day (no wash-sale rule in India, approx.); confirm on-time ITR for 8-year carry-forward
can_do.why: Direct tax alpha; LTCL only offsets LTCG

can_do.item: Executing third-party model feeds or 'technology consulting' inside NDPMS
can_do.what: Any external model that drives names, sizes or timing of NDPMS trades
can_do.why: Reg 24 bar on investing on another entity's advice; SEBI's May-2026 order penalised exactly this

can_do.item: Naked shorts, leverage, intraday or high-frequency overlays
can_do.what: Unhedged derivative shorts, borrowed funds, margin, intraday turnover
can_do.why: Prohibited today (2026 proposal on unhedged shorts not notified); NDPMS consent latency makes them uneconomic anyway

detailed_markdown:
# NDPMS ₹500 Cr Mandate — Regulatory Perimeter, Mandate Design and Tax Framework

Status date: 12 September 2026. Governing law: SEBI (Portfolio Managers) Regulations, 2020 ("PMS Regs") as amended, plus the Master Circular for Portfolio Managers dated 16 July 2025 (SEBI/HO/IMD/IMD-POD-1/P/CIR/2025/104) [1][3]. SEBI's consultation paper of 23 July 2026 proposing draft PMS Regulations 2026 (comments closed 13 Aug 2026) is NOT notified as far as we could verify; treat every item marked "2026 proposal" as pipeline, not law [11]. Primary SEBI/APMI hosts were unreachable from this environment; facts below were verified through secondary extracts of the primary documents and are cited; anything we could not pin down is marked "approx." or "verify".

## 1. Regulatory perimeter for NON-DISCRETIONARY PMS (NDPMS)

### 1.1 What NDPMS is, legally
- Discretionary PM "individually and independently manages" client funds; a non-discretionary PM "manages the funds in accordance with the directions of the client" (PMS Regs, Reg 2 definitions; Reg 24(1)-(2)) [1][2]. SEBI has not prescribed the form of a client direction. The regulatory floor is: no trade without a client direction that is evidenced, time-stamped and retrievable at inspection.
- Audit trail is mandatory for all PMs: time-stamping of order placement, execution and allocation; board-approved dealing-room policy; recorded dealing-room communications; automated order-management systems for PMs with AUM ≥ ₹1,000 Cr (Master Circular, dealing-room and order-placement chapter) [3]. For NDPMS the client instruction is the first link of that chain and must be captured in the same system.
- A PM "shall not invest client funds based on the advice of any other entity" (Reg 24, reported as 24(10)) and may not outsource core investment functions. SEBI's order of 26 May 2026 against First Global Finance (₹42 lakh penalty, 21-day onboarding bar) held that "investment decisions" include quantities, timing and client-level execution, not just model approval [12]. Implication: Ionic's own IC must own every recommendation in the NDPMS pack; third-party model feeds cannot drive the NDPMS book.

### 1.2 Eligible universe and hard limits (current law)

| Asset | NDPMS status | Rule / limit | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Listed equity, ETFs (equity, debt, gold, silver, international, liquid), listed REIT/InvIT, listed bonds/G-secs/SDLs, T-bills, CPs/CDs, money-market | Allowed | Core "listed securities and money-market instruments" universe; no cap | [1][2] |
| Mutual fund units (incl. index funds, active funds, FoFs, SIF units — SIFs sit under Chapter VI-C of the MF Regulations, min ₹10 lakh per PAN per AMC, live since 1-Apr-2025) | Allowed | Direct plans only; no distribution-related fee may be charged to the client on MF units; management fee per agreement is permitted | [3][16][33] |
| Unlisted securities: AIF units (Cat I/II/III), unlisted REIT/InvIT units, unlisted debt, pre-IPO/unlisted shares, warrants | Allowed, capped | ≤ 25% of the client's AUM for NDPMS/advisory (Reg 24(4)); discretionary PMS may not hold unlisted at all. "Active" breach (incl. subscribing to a rights issue) is non-compliance; "passive" breach (price move/redemption) must be cured — cure window approx. 90 days, verify | [1][2] |
| Same, for a Large Value Accredited Investor (LVAI) | Allowed up to 100% | Cap lifted for LVAI clients, subject to Disclosure Document disclosure and bilateral terms | [6][7] |
| Exchange-traded derivatives (equity index/stock F&O, commodity derivatives) | Allowed, restricted | Only for hedging and portfolio rebalancing; total derivative exposure ≤ portfolio funds placed with the PM; PM "shall not leverage" the portfolio; custodian required before commodity derivatives | [3][2] |
| Short selling / naked shorts | Not allowed | No unhedged short exposure today (2026 proposal: ≤ 50% of AUM via equity ETDs, within a 1.25x total-exposure cap and 10% option-premium cap, with explicit client consent — not notified) | [11] |
| Securities lending | Allowed | Lending only through the SEBI SLB mechanism (Reg 24 carve-out); requires client direction under NDPMS | [1][2] |
| Borrowing / margin / leverage | Not allowed | PM shall not borrow on behalf of clients; "invest, not borrow" | [2][3] |
| Foreign securities (direct US/UK stocks, offshore funds) | Not allowed inside PMS AUM today | 2026 proposal would permit "specified foreign securities" (listed equity, listed debt, regulated funds) — pipeline only. Route today: client's own LRS/OPI outside NDPMS AUM | [11] |
| Third-party PMS strategies | Not investable inside NDPMS AUM | A PMS is a service contract, not a "security"; plus Reg 24 bar on investing on another entity's advice. Structure outside AUM (see 1.4) | [1][12] |
| Securities of Angel One group / associates | Allowed with one-time prior positive consent | Equity ≤ 15% single associate / 25% all; debt+hybrid ≤ 15% / 25%; combined equity+debt+hybrid ≤ 30% of client AUM; no unrated associate debt; hybrid = REIT/InvIT/convertibles; MF units excluded from the cap; disclosure in every periodic report | [4] |
| Gold/silver: ETFs, SGBs (secondary), gold MF/FoF | Allowed | Listed instruments; no PMS-specific cap | [1] |
| Cash / liquid / overnight / arbitrage funds | Allowed | Client funds in a separate scheduled-bank account; liquid/arbitrage via direct plans | [2][3] |

### 1.3 Fees, expenses and exit loads (current law)
- No upfront fee, directly or indirectly. Brokerage at actuals. Operating expenses (excluding brokerage) ≤ 0.50% p.a. of average daily AUM. Exit load ≤ 3% / 2% / 1% of redeemed amount in years 1/2/3, nil after 3 years. Performance fee only on a high-water-mark basis over the life of the investment; hurdle optional. Fee illustration (Master Circular Annexure 4A) and separately signed fee annexure with the client's typed/handwritten acknowledgement are mandatory at onboarding (digital mode allowed from 1-Oct-2024) [3][8][33].
- LVAI relaxations: Schedule IV (prescribed agreement contents) does not apply; exit-load quantum and manner are bilaterally negotiated [5][6]. Whether the 0.50% operating-expense cap and no-upfront-fee rule are also relaxed for LVAI is not explicit in the sources we could read — verify; our design assumes they still bind.
- GST 18% on management and performance fees; fees are generally NOT deductible against the client's capital gains (Mumbai ITAT, Devendra Kothari; contrary Pune/Delhi/Kolkata rulings; unsettled) [26].

### 1.4 Third-party PMS, group products and conflicts — how to actually structure
1. Third-party PMS sleeve: client signs directly with the external PM (own PMS agreement, own demat/bank sub-account). Ionic may be paid as distributor or advise via its advisory registration; distributor commission must be disclosed in the client's periodic report (Reg 31 report must show distributor commission) [31]. The sleeve sits OUTSIDE NDPMS AUM and outside our TWRR; it enters our "house book" only for consolidated risk/attribution reporting.
2. Where the strategy exists as an AIF Cat III or SIF, prefer the wrapper: units are securities and investable inside NDPMS (Cat III units count toward the 25% unlisted cap; SIF units are MF units and do not) — interpretation, verify with compliance.
3. Angel One group products (AMC schemes, any group AIF/SIF): stay inside the 15/25/30% associate limits with the Annexure A one-time consent; self-impose a tighter IPS cap (we recommend 10% of AUM) and require IC minutes evidencing best-in-class selection each time.

### 1.5 Custody, fund accounting, reporting obligations

| Obligation | Cadence / deadline | Notes | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Custodian for securities | Standing | Mandatory for PMs (historic <₹500 Cr AUM exemption; at ₹500 Cr+ it binds anyway); mandatory before commodity derivatives | [1][3] |
| Client funds in separate scheduled-bank account; securities not in PM's name | Standing | Client-name demat + bank; no pooling for this mandate | [3] |
| Report to client | ≤ every 3 months (Reg 31); we commit monthly | Composition/valuation, transactions, income received, expenses, risks, associate investments, distributor commission | [31][4] |
| Monthly report to SEBI (and APMI) | Within 7 working days of month-end | AUM, clients, performance by IA | [9] |
| Performance benchmarking | Monthly / per IA | TWRR per Investment Approach; APMI-listed benchmark per strategy tag; from 1-Apr-2023 | [9] |
| Firm-level performance audit | Annual; confirmation to SEBI within 60 days of FY-end | Covers DPMS and NDPMS; APMI standard ToR from 1-Oct-2023 | [10] |
| Debt/MM valuation | Daily | Prices from APMI-empanelled agencies (CRISIL, ICRA Analytics, NSE Indices) | [32] |
| Disclosure Document | Filed with SEBI; updated on material change; CA-certified | Must disclose unlisted-to-100% LVAI terms, associate exposure, derivatives use | [1][7] |
| Digital onboarding | Standing | E-signed agreement; typed fee acknowledgement; APMI standard procedure | [8] |
| Alert-based monitoring of associate limits | Real-time | Required by 2022 amendment | [4] |

### 1.6 2025–2026 changes that matter here
- Co-investment: AIF (Second Amendment) Regs 2025 + circular SEBI/HO/AFD/AFD-POD-1/P/CIR/2025/126 (9-Sep-2025) allow Co-Investment Vehicle (CIV) schemes inside the AIF, restricted to accredited investors, one scheme per investment, ring-fenced, no leverage; the older Co-investment Portfolio Manager (CPMS) route under PMS Regs (Nov 2021) remains [13][34]. Accreditation is therefore the key to co-investing.
- Accredited-investor framework: income ≥ ₹2 Cr, or net worth ≥ ₹7.5 Cr (≥ ₹3.75 Cr financial), or income ≥ ₹1 Cr + net worth ≥ ₹5 Cr (≥ ₹2.5 Cr financial); SEBI (Sept 2025 board memo) proposed a ₹5 Cr securities-market-assets route for individuals and ₹20 Cr for corporates/trusts and manager-led accreditation; Jan 9, 2026 circular changed net-worth certificate format [15]. LVF minimum proposed to fall from ₹70 Cr to ₹25 Cr; Dec 2025 circular gives AI-only scheme relaxations [14].
- Digital onboarding eased (May 2024, effective 1-Oct-2024) [8]. PMS business-transfer framework (Oct 2025) [3].
- 2026 consultation (23-Jul-2026): to-be-listed securities; discretionary PMS up to 10% in investment-grade unlisted debt; specified foreign securities; MF-PMS tier (₹25 lakh ticket, ₹2 Cr net worth) managing only direct MF plans incl. ETFs and SIFs; derivatives to 1.25x with unhedged shorts to 50% and option premium 10%; independent fund managers under registered PMs [11]. No change to the NDPMS 25% cap or to consent mechanics was reported.

## 2. Large-value accredited investor route — on-board under it

| Question | Answer |
|---|---|
| Threshold | Accredited investor + agreement ≥ ₹10 Cr with the PM = LVAI [5][6] |

## 5. Mandate design: IPS and NDPMS agreement that runs monthly without per-trade friction

### 5.1 Legal architecture
1. LVAI NDPMS Agreement (bespoke; Schedule IV not mandatory) with annexes: (A) IPS and SAA bands; (B) Consent Protocol; (C) Standing Instructions Register; (D) Fee annexure with SEBI illustration; (E) Associate-investment consent (SEBI Annexure A format); (F) Derivatives/hedging protocol; (G) SLB authorisation; (H) Reporting pack spec.
2. Consent Protocol (Annex B): the monthly Rebalance Proposal Pack (RPP) is the "direction of the client". It lists every trade (ISIN, side, quantity or ₹ amount, limit/participation rule, execution window, rationale, cost and tax estimate). The client approves the pack as a whole or line-by-line by e-sign (Aadhaar/DSC) on the portal, or by email from registered IDs. Validity: 10 trading days; unexecuted lines lapse. Amendments require a new approval. All approvals are hashed and stored with the OMS audit trail.
3. Standing Instructions Register (Annex C) — narrow, mechanical, revocable, each with trigger, instrument, quantity rule, validity and maximum ₹: (i) sweep idle cash > ₹50 lakh into a named liquid/overnight fund daily; (ii) reinvest distributions into the same instrument or the liquid fund; (iii) default corporate-action elections (dividend reinvest off; rights subscribe only if pre-approved in RPP because a rights subscription is an "active" unlisted-cap event); (iv) execute already-approved tranche schedules (e.g., ₹20 Cr/week into a named ETF for 5 Thursdays); (v) auto-roll of an approved hedge into the next monthly series at same notional. Anything that changes asset-class weights or names a new security stays in the RPP.
4. Legal risk: a "pre-approved model with bands where the PM picks timing/size" drifts toward discretion and risks recharacterisation at inspection. Mitigation: standing instructions are limit-order-like (fully specified), client can revoke on the portal, and we obtain a legal opinion and consider SEBI Informal Guidance before go-live. Status: unclear_verify.

### 5.4 CAN / SHOULD / AVOID in this domain
- CAN: invest across every listed class, MF/ETF/SIF direct plans, AIFs to 25% (100% under LVAI), hedge with F&O within 1x exposure, lend via SLB, hold securities in the client's own demat under our custodian, report monthly, charge fixed + HWM performance fees, negotiate exit load and agreement form under LVAI.
- SHOULD: on-board every entity as LVAI; build the RPP e-consent portal with hashed audit trail; run 2–3 purpose-segregated demat accounts for FIFO management; keep unlisted ≤ 15% and associates ≤ 10% by IPS; pre-approve tail-hedge protocol monthly; get legal opinion/informal guidance on standing instructions; adopt APMI benchmark tagging and compute NDPMS TWRR daily; book the third-party PMS and LRS sleeves outside AUM with look-through reporting; run a March tax-loss/lot review; file for CIV eligibility via accreditation.
- AVOID: any discretion "in practice" (PM choosing names/sizes after a generic approval); executing third-party model feeds inside NDPMS; debt MFs for long-horizon fixed income (slab tax); unlisted debt; naked shorts or leverage; upfront fees; distribution fees on MF units; buying international ETFs at > 1% premium; letting rights issues push unlisted over 25% ("active" breach); intraday/high-frequency anything; pooling this client's assets with others.

risks_and_pitfalls: Recharacterisation risk: a 'pre-approved model + bands' where the PM chooses names, sizes or timing can be treated by SEBI inspectors as de-facto discretionary management under a non-discretionary label (mis-registration of the Investment Approach, misreporting). Mitigation: fully specified, revocable standing instructions; legal opinion; consider SEBI Informal Guidance.

Reg 24 'advice of another entity' / outsourcing breach if any third-party model, quant vendor or group research feed effectively drives NDPMS trades — SEBI's 26-May-2026 First Global order (₹42 lakh, onboarding bar) defines investment decisions to include quantities, timing and client-level execution.

Active breach of the 25% unlisted cap through rights subscriptions, AIF capital calls or CIV drawdowns while listed assets fall in a drawdown; only passive breaches get a cure window. Entities not on-boarded as LVAI are exposed; keep a 10-pt buffer and route every rights/drawdown through the RPP.

Associate-limit breach (15/25/30%) via large purchases of Angel One group ETFs/MF-linked hybrids or group InvIT/REIT units; alert-based monitoring must be pre-trade, and the one-time consent form must be in the SEBI Annexure A format.

Consent latency in stress: client unavailable during a 10%+ drawdown leaves hedges un-rolled or cash undeployed; ₹25 Cr mis-weight at 1% daily vol costs ~₹79 lakh (1σ) over 10 days. Mitigate via 2-day SLA, escalation, and pre-approved hedge-roll standing instruction.

International sleeve fragility: USD 7 bn MF overseas cap near exhaustion (May–Jun 2026) closes FoF windows and pushes Indian-listed international ETFs to 5–15% premiums that collapse when creations resume; LRS/IFSC routes sit outside AUM and outside our TWRR.
FIFO per demat account destroys tax-aware rebalancing if all holdings sit in one demat; the multi-demat workaround needs custodian and reporting support and must be reflected in the client agreement.

Tax-rule drift mid-mandate: Income-tax Act 2025 renumbering (112A→198 etc.), Budget 2026 narrowing of the SGB exemption to primary subscribers, REIT/InvIT dividend change pending enactment verification, and debt-MF slab taxation make historical tax assumptions unreliable; annual tax-matrix refresh required.
Cat III AIF fund-level taxation (F&O/business income at ~39–42.7% MMR) and higher F&O STT from 1-Apr-2026 erode long-short returns; prefer SIF wrappers where available.
TCS drag on LRS (20% above ₹10 lakh, refundable only via ITR) and the USD 250k ceiling make the offshore sleeve slow to build; family entities must each remit.

Pipeline regulatory change: draft PMS Regulations 2026 (foreign securities, 1.25x derivatives, unhedged shorts, to-be-listed securities, MF-PMS) may be notified during the mandate; the agreement needs a 'change in law' clause to re-paper consent scope without a new onboarding.

Fee-deductibility disputes: PMS fees generally not deductible against capital gains (Mumbai ITAT line), so the client's after-tax alpha is lower than the pre-fee TWRR suggests; disclose in the fee annexure.

Reporting errors: NDPMS TWRR must be included in the annual firm-level performance audit and in monthly SEBI/APMI filings; outside-AUM sleeves must be excluded from regulatory TWRR but included in client look-through — two parallel performance books with reconciliation risk.
Exit-load and fee negotiation under LVAI could be challenged if opex cap or no-upfront-fee rules are found to still bind; our design assumes they bind — verify before signing any deviation.

Custody and segregation: any pooling of this client's cash or securities with other PMS clients, or holding securities in the PM's name, is a segregation breach; insist on client-name demat and bank accounts under the custodian.
open_questions: Which legal entities will hold the ₹500 Cr (individuals, HUF, family trust, holding company, LLP)? Each must independently qualify as an accredited investor and sign an NDPMS agreement ≥ ₹10 Cr for LVAI status; entity choice also determines tax rate (39% slab vs 25.17% company) and FEMA route (LRS vs OPI).

Does the client accept a monthly Rebalance Proposal Pack with a 2-business-day consent SLA and a 10-trading-day validity, and who are the authorised signatories/e-sign holders (including a backup) for the portal?

Which mechanical actions will the client pre-authorise in the Standing Instructions Register (cash sweep threshold, distribution reinvestment, tranche schedules, hedge rolls), and will the client accept our legal position (or do they want SEBI Informal Guidance first)?
What is the client's tolerance for Angel One group products (IPS cap proposed 10% vs SEBI 30%), and will the client sign the SEBI Annexure A related-party consent at onboarding?

Does the client already hold securities to be transferred in-specie, with cost and acquisition dates available, and are there legacy SGBs (secondary-market purchases now taxable on redemption after Budget 2026)?

Which international route does the client prefer: family LRS into GIFT-IFSC funds (outside AUM, ~₹2.2 Cr per adult per year), holding-company OPI, or Indian-listed international ETFs inside AUM with a premium cap? What is the desired look-through reporting of outside-AUM sleeves?
Will the client permit securities lending (SLB) on core holdings and a standing tail-hedge budget of up to 1% of AUM per year via Nifty put spreads?

Fee terms: fixed 0.30% + 10% over the 80/20 house benchmark with HWM and annual crystallisation, nil exit load with 30-day notice — acceptable? Does the client want the performance fee base to exclude cash/liquid?

Should the IPS cap total unlisted exposure at 15% (our recommendation) or use the LVAI headroom for a larger private-credit/PE programme, accepting illiquidity and drawdown-timing breach risk for any non-LVAI entity?
Will the client agree to purpose-segregated demat accounts (Core/Tactical/Income) and separate MF folios to manage FIFO, and does their tax adviser accept this approach?
Which third-party PMS strategies (if any) does the client want, and does the client accept that these sit outside NDPMS AUM under direct agreements with disclosed distributor commission?
Does the IC want to adopt the draft 2026 provisions (foreign securities, 1.25x derivatives) automatically upon notification via a change-in-law clause, or re-consent each time?
